Machine Systems — Foundation Lesson

Understand the relationship between power source, transmission, actuator, sensor and controller inside a mechanical system.

How a machine becomes a system

A machine system is more than one component. It is a coordinated set of parts that converts energy into controlled work. GPSJ keeps the physical object, the scientific explanation, simulation and practice in the same environment.

Core relationship: energy source → transmission → actuator → physical motion → sensor feedback → controller correction.

1. Power source

The source supplies energy to the machine. Depending on the system, this may be electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, thermal or another lawful engineering source.

2. Transmission

Gears, belts, shafts, couplings and related components transfer motion and torque from one part of the machine to another.

3. Actuator

The actuator converts supplied energy into controlled movement. Examples include electric motors and hydraulic or pneumatic actuators.

4. Sensor and feedback

Sensors measure what actually happened. Their measurements allow a controller to compare the real state with the desired state and make corrections.

GPSJ safety rule: learning and simulation can precede supervised testing. Real-world control remains role-, authorization-, device- and jurisdiction-dependent.
